detailed_rationale:
Skipper Ltd manufactures power transmission and telecom towers (T&D structures), polymer pipes and fittings, and executes EPC infrastructure projects, exporting to 60+ countries alongside a large domestic utility/telecom customer base. It is a direct beneficiary of India's ongoing transmission-grid capex cycle (grid strengthening, renewable-energy evacuation infrastructure, and rising power demand from data centers and industry).

FY26 sales came in at ~Rs.5,553cr, roughly 20% growth on a TTM basis, with quarterly profit ranging Rs.37-78cr over the last four quarters (Q4 FY26 the strongest at Rs.78cr). ROCE (~23%) and current-run-rate ROE (~16.5%) are healthy, ahead of the more dated figures in the quant dataset, consistent with margin improvement as the order book scales. The company raised fresh equity capital in July 2026 (~92.23 lakh shares at Rs.470, raising ~Rs.433.5cr) and CRISIL upgraded its long-term rating to A+/Stable the same month -- both constructive signals about balance-sheet trajectory. That said, debtor days have lengthened (~79 to ~98 days) and free cash flow was negative in FY26 despite profitable operations, reflecting the working-capital and capex intensity typical of EPC/tower manufacturing businesses serving utility and government customers, with CWIP (capital work-in-progress) up meaningfully as new capacity comes online. Total borrowings rose from ~Rs.740cr to ~Rs.948cr before the July capital raise, which should help delever going forward.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold and our research confirms a genuinely improving, capex-cycle-driven growth story with no red flags beyond the ordinary working-capital and leverage dynamics of an EPC/manufacturing business scaling up -- the recent equity raise and rating upgrade are constructive counterweights. Hold stands; nothing here rises to a rescue-worthy or escalation-worthy level.
summary: Skipper is a transmission-tower and infrastructure-pipe manufacturer riding India's power-grid capex upcycle, with solid revenue growth, improving returns, a recent equity capital raise, and a credit-rating upgrade. Working capital has stretched a bit as the order book has grown, which is normal for this kind of business serving utility and government clients. We rate it a Hold: the growth runway looks genuine, but the stock already reflects a good part of that optimism.
positive_para: Skipper sits squarely in India's transmission and distribution capex supercycle -- grid strengthening, renewable-energy evacuation infrastructure, and rising power demand all support multi-year order-book growth for tower and EPC players. Revenue and profitability have both been growing, ROCE is healthy at ~23%, and the company has taken proactive balance-sheet steps (a ~Rs.433.5cr equity raise and a CRISIL rating upgrade to A+/Stable in July 2026) that reduce financing risk as it scales.
negative_para: Working capital strain is real and worth watching: debtor days have lengthened from ~79 to ~98 days, and free cash flow was negative in FY26 despite reported profitability, a combination typical of EPC/infrastructure suppliers with government and utility customers but one that limits self-funded growth. Debt rose meaningfully before the recent capital raise, and revenue growth has decelerated from the stronger 3-year trailing pace to a more moderate ~20% most recently -- the business needs to keep converting its order book into cash, not just booked revenue.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a PE in the high-20s, the market is pricing continued execution of the T&D capex cycle at a healthy growth rate; given the genuine sector tailwind and the recent balance-sheet strengthening (equity raise, rating upgrade), this looks close to fair value rather than clearly cheap or clearly rich, provided working-capital conversion improves alongside revenue growth.
